claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'd like to find out if I can claim Child Benefit. I have one child - my son Alex. He's 18 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Since Alex is 18 years old, I need to ask a few more questions to determine your eligibility.

For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit can usually continue if they stay in approved education or training.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training? This would include things like:
- A-levels or equivalent
- Scottish Highers
- NVQs up to level 3
- A course at a college or university that isn't a higher education course (like a degree)

Or has he perhaps registered with a careers service or the armed services after leaving education?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is still in education. He's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great, thank you! Studying A-levels at sixth form college counts as approved education, which is good news for your eligibility.

Just a couple more questions to confirm your situation:

Do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. And just to confirm a couple more things:

Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex? And is Alex working 24 hours or more per week, or receiving any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex. And yes, actually, he does receive Universal Credit in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know about the Universal Credit. This is an important detail.

Unfortunately, one of the rules for Child Benefit is that you'll stop receiving it if your child starts getting certain benefits in their own right, and Universal Credit is one of those benefits.

Even though Alex is in approved education (studying A-levels), the fact that he receives Universal Credit in his own name means you would not be eligible for Child Benefit for him.

Let me provide you with my final assessment:

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm sorry to say that **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**Here's why:**

Although Alex meets several of the usual criteria:
- ✅ He lives with you in the UK
- ✅ He's under 20 and in approved education (A-levels)
- ✅ No one else is claiming Child Benefit for him

**However**, because Alex receives **Universal Credit in his own name**, this disqualifies you from receiving Child Benefit for him. The rules state that Child Benefit stops if a child starts getting certain benefits in their own right, including Universal Credit.

If Alex's circumstances change in the future (for example, if he stops receiving Universal Credit), you may wish to revisit your eligibility at that time.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
